findings.description: The remedy the amendment gives for reopening an abandoned PR (`pup merge <session> --pr`) is refused by planRegate whenever the PR head did not move, and its message says to merge on GitHub and `pup land`. The freed ADR number then lands twice without any check.
findings.body:
**Concern.** The amendment accepts that a reopened PR goes unchecked until it is re-gated, and names the remedy: *"the operator who reopens an abandoned PR re-gates it with `pup merge <session> --pr` before merging it, and that re-gate refuses the clash."* A plain reopen does not move the PR head. `planRegate` refuses exactly that case before any stage runs, so no `merge` event is written and the ADR-number stage never runs:

```ts
if (pr.head === pinned) {
  throw new Error(
    `${prUrl} still has its head at ${pinned}, the commit the gate pinned: there is nothing ` +
      `new to gate. Merge it on GitHub, then run \`pup land ${sanitizeReason(sessionId)}\`. ` +
```

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/bf7cb4b8131aad22264485c43e5b1739f39a790b/src/core/regate.service.ts#L124-L129

**Trigger.**
1. Session X's PR adds `0150-*.md`. The operator runs `pup land X --abandon-closed`, and `isClosedOut` drops X from `competingBranches`.
2. Session Y gates its own `0150-*.md`, and that PR merges.
3. The operator reopens X's PR and runs `pup merge X --pr`, as the ADR says.
4. `mergeToRegate` → `planRegate` refuses with "nothing new to gate. Merge it on GitHub, then run `pup land X`". The operator does that.
5. `newestMerge` skips `pr_closed`, so `pup land X` lands. `land.service.ts` runs no ADR-number check.

Result: two decision-0150 files on the target. Before this PR a closed PR counted forever, so Y's gate would have refused 0150 and this path could not happen.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/bf7cb4b8131aad22264485c43e5b1739f39a790b/docs/adr/0146-the-gate-refuses-an-adr-number-the-target-or.md#L181-L193

**Fix direction (either one).**
- Let `planRegate` re-gate an unmoved head when the session's newest `merge`/`pr_closed` event is `pr_closed`. That re-gate's `merge` event makes the claim count again.
- Or have `pup land` refuse a session whose newest `merge`/`pr_closed` event is `pr_closed` until a re-gate records a new merge.

Either way, the amendment's text must match the path you choose.

findings.description: `pup land --abandon-closed` treats a `MergeLockLostError` like any other refusal. If the lock is lost, the operator is never told that the `pr_closed` event was already written and the PR's ADR numbers are already freed. `pup land` and `pup retire` report what happened before they fail on a lost lock.

The `isClosedOut` and `competingBranches` JSDocs say a `pup land` that read the PR CLOSED records the close. A plain `pup land` of a CLOSED PR refuses and records nothing; only the operator's `pup land --abandon-closed` writes `pr_closed`.
findings.body:
**Concern.** Two JSDocs describe the model the second commit rejected. The `isClosedOut` JSDoc says `pr_closed` comes from "(`pup land` reading the PR CLOSED)" (L194-195). The `competingBranches` JSDoc says the close is recorded "by `pup retire` or by a `pup land` that read it CLOSED" (L208-209).

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/bf7cb4b8131aad22264485c43e5b1739f39a790b/src/core/adr-number.service.ts#L192-L209

In the code, `landSession` throws on `pr.state === 'CLOSED'` and writes nothing ([land.service.ts](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/bf7cb4b8131aad22264485c43e5b1739f39a790b/src/core/land.service.ts#L109-L118)). The only writer of `pr_closed` is `abandonClosedSession`, which is reached through `--abandon-closed`. A maintainer who trusts these docs would expect a plain land to free a closed PR's numbers. That is exactly the session-closes-a-peer's-PR hole ADR 0146's amendment closes, and the docs invite "restoring" it.

**Fix.** Lines 194-195:
```
 * retired or pr_closed event is `retired` (`pup retire`) or `pr_closed`
 * (`pup land --abandon-closed`).
```
Lines 208-209: replace "by a `pup land` that read it CLOSED" with "by `pup land --abandon-closed`".

The test title at `src/core/adr-number.test.ts:349` ("ignores a PR peer pup land read closed") has the same wording, for example "ignores a PR peer abandoned with pup land --abandon-closed, even once its gated commit is pruned".

findings.description: `openPullRequest` stops at `landed`/`retired` but not at the new `pr_closed`. So after `pup land --abandon-closed`, the inbox still shows the abandoned PR as "PR opened, not landed", and no honest command clears it. Adding `|| row.type === 'pr_closed'` (and updating its JSDoc) would clear it, and a later re-gate's `merge` would show the PR again.

The call-site comment "Any session can close a peer's PR with the shared gh login…" restates `abandonClosedSession`'s JSDoc. `docs/conventions/general.md` §Comments (seam-duplication test) says a duplicated call-site WHY comment should go. The same applies to the comment above the CLOSED refusal in `landSession`.

`abandonClosedSession` scans `listEvents` for a prior `pr_closed` only to return `recorded: false`. `isClosedOut` reads only the newest event, so appending unconditionally would remove the scan, the `recorded` field, and the CLI's second message, at the cost of one duplicate row per repeated run.
